title: Derive status from lifecycle instead of storing it
outcome: A Change states where it stands once, in change.json's lifecycle. The coarse status is computed from it by a table the compiler keeps exhaustive, so the two can no longer disagree.
acceptanceCriteria: change-types.ts exports statusOf(lifecycle) backed by a Record<ChangeLifecycle, ChangeStatus>; removing a key from that record fails type-check, which is the check that the derivation cannot go stale.
The mapping reproduces today's grouping exactly: discussing to discussing, archived to archived, the other seven to in-progress. No Change changes bucket on the rendered catalog.
change.schema.json no longer lists status in properties or required, and no change.json in the repository carries a status field.
parseChangeMetadata takes no status argument, computes status with statusOf, and requires archivedAt when lifecycle is archived rather than when status is archived.
lifecycleMatchesStatus is deleted, and change-metadata.test.ts covers the archived-lifecycle requirement and the rejection of an unknown lifecycle value.
